title: Chain inspection: Proof strip
topics: Linked lists, binary trees and search trees
summary: Linked traversal. Return the whole list.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`head` is the first node of a linked list. In examples, [4, 7] means nodes 4 then 7, linked in that order. [] means no nodes. The runner builds the nodes for you.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `values`. `head` is the first node of a linked list. A node holds a number in val and a link to the next node in next. Follow next until there are no more nodes. Record each val in order. The list has no loops. An empty list gives an empty `values`.
2. Complete `chainInspectionProofStrip` so it returns `values`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `head` is [3, 5, 4, 4, -4], then `values` is [3, 5, 4, 4, -4] and `chainInspectionProofStrip` returns [3, 5, 4, 4, -4].

Rules
- If `values` is empty, return [].

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `head` is [17, 18, -4, 0, 18].
TEST DATA 2: `head` is [-6, 6, 6, 6].

Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the number of nodes. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.

referenceSolutions.python:
def chainInspectionProofStrip(head):
    a=head
    out=[]
    node=a
    while node:
        out.append(node.val)
        node=node.next
    return out
